nodes.name: Virginia Tech Institute for Advanced Computing
nodes.description: Virginia Tech's graduate research institute in Academic Building One, 3625 Potomac Ave, Potomac Yard (opened spring 2025; formerly branded the Innovation Campus). Next G Wireless is one of its four research areas: AI-native wireless, joint sensing and communications, mmWave/THz, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, distributed MIMO and O-RAN. Wireless lab on the 3rd floor.

nodes.name: Wireless@Virginia Tech
nodes.description: Virginia Tech's wireless research centre (30+ faculty), led from Blacksburg. Its director, Lingjia Liu, is core faculty in Alexandria.

nodes.name: VT National Security Institute
nodes.description: Virginia Tech institute working with the Alexandria institute on NextG, including the DoD Mobile dMIMO project.

nodes.name: Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation (VT-ARC)
nodes.description: Virginia Tech's applied research affiliate in Arlington. Selected as the Technical Program Office for ATIS' Next G Alliance, which runs the North American 6G roadmap work.

nodes.name: Commonwealth Cyber Initiative (CCI) & xG Testbed
nodes.description: State-funded network of 40+ Virginia institutions led by Virginia Tech. Its xG Testbed at the Virginia Tech Research Center in Arlington is an O-RAN Alliance Open Testing and Integration Center (OTIC). Member of the Next G Alliance, O-RAN Alliance and National Spectrum Consortium.
nodes.address: Virginia Tech Research Center, 900 N Glebe Rd, Arlington, VA 22203

nodes.name: George Mason University
nodes.description: Leads the CCI Northern Virginia node and runs the Living Innovation Lab in Arlington with commercial-grade NextG/O-RAN testbeds. Part of the OTIC team and a WISPER university.

nodes.name: University of Arizona
nodes.description: WISPER partner university.

nodes.name: MIT
nodes.description: Next G Alliance contributing member. Collaborates with Lingjia Liu's lab on AI-native wireless.

nodes.name: Duke University
nodes.description: Collaborates with Lingjia Liu's lab on AI-native wireless prototypes.

nodes.name: National Science Foundation (NSF)
nodes.description: Headquartered in Alexandria since 2017. Staying in the city but moving from 2415 Eisenhower Ave to 401 Dulany St (the USPTO campus) as HUD takes over its old building. Main federal funder of NextG research: RINGS, SpectrumX and the WISPER industry-university centre.
nodes.address: 401 Dulany St, Alexandria, VA 22314 (relocating from 2415 Eisenhower Ave)

nodes.name: Institute for Defense Analyses (IDA)
nodes.description: Federally funded research centre at 4850 Mark Center Drive, Alexandria. Has published analysis for the DoD on the implications of 5G and next-generation mobile networks.

nodes.name: DoD FutureG Office (OUSD R&E)
nodes.description: Pentagon office responsible for strategic assessment and R&D of FutureG (5G/6G). Funds work through the National Spectrum Consortium and direct awards, such as Virginia Tech's $9M Mobile dMIMO project.

nodes.name: NTIA (Dept of Commerce)
nodes.description: Runs the Public Wireless Supply Chain Innovation Fund, which funded the $42M ACCoRD O-RAN project and Virginia Tech O-RAN research. Supports SpectrumX.
nodes.address: Herbert C. Hoover Building, 1401 Constitution Ave NW, Washington, DC

nodes.name: NIST
nodes.description: Federal partner in the NSF RINGS NextG programme.

nodes.name: FCC
nodes.description: Supports the NSF Spectrum Innovation Initiative behind SpectrumX.

nodes.name: Commonwealth of Virginia
nodes.description: Funds the Commonwealth Cyber Initiative and invested in Virginia Tech's Alexandria campus, part of the Amazon HQ2 talent package.

nodes.name: Alexandria Economic Development Partnership (AEDP)
nodes.description: The city's economic development partnership. Championed the Virginia Tech campus and Potomac Yard Metro, and worked to keep NSF in Alexandria.

nodes.name: JBG SMITH
nodes.description: Developer of National Landing and North Potomac Yard alongside Virginia Tech. Holds licensed CBRS spectrum covering Arlington and the City of Alexandria, deployed with Federated Wireless.

nodes.name: Amazon (HQ2)
nodes.description: HQ2 in National Landing, two miles from the Virginia Tech campus. The campus was part of the package that won HQ2 for Northern Virginia.

nodes.name: Ericsson
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member, RINGS partner, WISPER industry member, ACCoRD partner and Open Generation Consortium member.

nodes.name: Nokia / Nokia Federal / Bell Labs
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member, RINGS partner, ACCoRD partner. Nokia Federal leads a RAPID ISAC award via the National Spectrum Consortium. Bell Labs gave the first Innovation Campus distinguished lecture on 6G.

nodes.name: Samsung
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member and ACCoRD partner.

nodes.name: Qualcomm
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member and RINGS partner.

nodes.name: InterDigital
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member. Chairs the WISPER Industry Advisory Board.

nodes.name: Keysight Technologies
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member and WISPER industry member.

nodes.name: Intel
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member, RINGS partner and ACCoRD partner.

nodes.name: Apple
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member and RINGS partner.

nodes.name: Google
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member and RINGS partner.

nodes.name: Microsoft
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member and RINGS partner.

nodes.name: NVIDIA
nodes.description: Research partner of Virginia Tech on AI for wireless (GPU-accelerated RAN). Hosted Lingjia Liu at GTC Washington DC 2025. Partner in Booz Allen's AI WIN initiative.

nodes.name: Mavenir
nodes.description: ACCoRD O-RAN project partner.

nodes.name: Fujitsu
nodes.description: ACCoRD O-RAN project partner.

nodes.name: Parallel Wireless
nodes.description: Leads a RAPID ISAC award with Andro and Virginia Tech (Nov 2026).

nodes.name: DeepSig
nodes.description: Arlington-based AI-native wireless software company. Awarded FutureG work through the National Spectrum Consortium, and part of the Nokia Federal RAPID team.

nodes.name: Federated Wireless
nodes.description: Arlington-based CBRS and private wireless provider. Partner of JBG SMITH on private wireless across National Landing and Alexandria.

nodes.name: COMSovereign
nodes.description: Donated commercial-grade O-RAN and 5G/NextG testbeds to the CCI Living Innovation Lab.

nodes.name: AT&T
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member. Co-leads ACCoRD. Part of the Nokia Federal RAPID team.

nodes.name: Verizon
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member, ACCoRD co-lead, Open Generation Consortium member.

nodes.name: T-Mobile
nodes.description: Next G Alliance founding member.

nodes.name: Lockheed Martin
nodes.description: Industry partner on Virginia Tech's Mobile dMIMO FutureG project (Advanced Technology Laboratories). WISPER industry member.

nodes.name: Northrop Grumman
nodes.description: WISPER industry member. Funds quantum research at the Alexandria institute.

nodes.name: RTX
nodes.description: WISPER industry member.

nodes.name: BAE Systems
nodes.description: WISPER industry member.

nodes.name: General Dynamics Mission Systems
nodes.description: WISPER industry member.

nodes.name: Booz Allen Hamilton
nodes.description: Collaborates with CCI and Virginia Tech on NTIA-funded O-RAN projects. Runs the AI Wireless Innovation Networks (AI WIN) initiative with NVIDIA and MITRE.

nodes.name: MITRE
nodes.description: Partner in the AI WIN spectrum demonstrations.

nodes.name: Peraton Labs
nodes.description: RAPID ISAC awardee via the National Spectrum Consortium.

nodes.name: ATIS Next G Alliance
nodes.description: ATIS initiative (Washington DC) for North American 6G leadership. Publishes the Roadmap to 6G. Membership tiers: Full, Contributing, Government and Strategic. VT-ARC runs its Technical Program Office.
nodes.address: ATIS, 1200 G St NW, Washington, DC

nodes.name: O-RAN Alliance
nodes.description: Global alliance for open, intelligent RAN. Designated CCI's Arlington testbed as a North American OTIC.

nodes.name: National Spectrum Consortium
nodes.description: Roughly 400-member consortium holding the DoD's $2.5B Spectrum Forward OTA. Channels FutureG prototype awards to members.

nodes.name: WISPER (NSF Industry-University Center)
nodes.description: NSF IUCRC for secure, resilient Next G networks, led by Virginia Tech with George Mason and the University of Arizona. Industry members fund and steer projects.
nodes.address: Led from Virginia Tech, Blacksburg, VA

nodes.name: Open Generation Consortium
nodes.description: 5G/drone innovation consortium. Virginia Tech is a partner.

nodes.name: CTIA
nodes.description: US wireless industry association. Member of the Open Generation Consortium.

nodes.name: NSF RINGS
nodes.description: Resilient & Intelligent NextG Systems: about $40M public-private research programme run by NSF with DoD, NIST and industry partners.

nodes.name: SpectrumX
nodes.description: NSF's $25M national spectrum innovation centre, with NTIA and FCC support.

nodes.name: ACCoRD O-RAN project
nodes.description: $42M NTIA-funded O-RAN testing project announced at the Virginia Tech Research Center, Arlington. CCI xG Testbed is its DC-area home.

nodes.name: Mobile dMIMO (FutureG)
nodes.description: $9M DoD FutureG project led by Virginia Tech, now worked on in the Alexandria wireless lab with Lockheed Martin.

nodes.name: RAPID ISAC awards
nodes.description: Eleven awards (over $50M, Nov 2026) from the National Spectrum Consortium and the FutureG Office for integrated sensing and communications prototypes for 5G/6G.

nodes.name: AI WIN
nodes.description: Booz Allen's AI Wireless Innovation Networks initiative with NVIDIA and MITRE, focused on spectrum agility for 6G.

nodes.name: Lingjia Liu
nodes.description: Professor, core faculty at the Alexandria institute and director (now co-director) of Wireless@Virginia Tech. Leads Mobile dMIMO. Research: 6G, AI for wireless, O-RAN, spectrum sharing.

nodes.name: Walid Saad
nodes.description: Professor and Next-G wireless lead at the Alexandria institute. Leads the NEWS group.

nodes.name: Kirk Cameron
nodes.description: Faculty lead and managing director, Virginia Tech Institute for Advanced Computing.
nodes.role: Managing director, VT Institute for Advanced Computing

nodes.name: Lance Collins
nodes.description: Virginia Tech's Washington DC area vice president.
nodes.role: Vice president, Washington DC area, Virginia Tech

nodes.name: Eric Burger
nodes.description: Chair of the Next G Alliance Research Council and its Technical Program Director. Research professor at CCI and Virginia Tech.
nodes.role: Chair, Next G Alliance Research Council

nodes.name: Luiz DaSilva
nodes.description: Executive director of CCI and director of WISPER.

nodes.name: Tom Rondeau
nodes.description: Principal Director, DoD FutureG Office.

nodes.name: Stephanie Landrum
nodes.description: President and CEO, Alexandria Economic Development Partnership.

nodes.name: Robert Gazda
nodes.description: Senior director of wireless research at InterDigital. Inaugural chair of the WISPER Industry Advisory Board.
nodes.role: Senior director of wireless research, InterDigital

nodes.name: Gus Anderson
nodes.description: Fellow, Lockheed Martin Advanced Technology Laboratories. Industry lead on Mobile dMIMO.

nodes.name: Daniel Jakubisin
nodes.description: Research associate professor, VT National Security Institute. Works on Mobile dMIMO.

nodes.name: Jaydee Griffith
nodes.description: Managing Director of ATIS' Next G Alliance. Previously Chief Technologist for NTIA's $1.5B Public Wireless Supply Chain Innovation Fund, and earlier at NTIA's Institute for Telecommunication Sciences working on 5G architecture standards and testing.
nodes.role: Managing Director, ATIS Next G Alliance
